job: JOB 1: Entrance sign band, gold lettering DEEPSLATE HOLDINGS / COMMUNITY SERVICES
why: The gold lettering band is placed in the right spot, but at this scale it reads as scattered gold blocks and orange teeth along the lintel rather than legible DEEPSLATE HOLDINGS text. It adds a little colour but not the crafted sign from the concept, and it doesn't break the silhouette.

job: JOB 2: Timber pilasters proud of the wall, dark quoins on the corners
why: The before and after renders are nearly identical, with only a few extra dark quoin blocks and slightly thicker pilaster tops, so the change adds no visible depth and does no harm.

job: JOB 3: Window sills / planter boxes with a timber front
why: The planter boxes gain a patterned timber front (slatted/trapdoor-style face) that adds relief and finish under the windows, matching the concept's crafted sills without altering the silhouette or adding clutter.

job: JOB 4: Window mullions and glazing bars
why: The upper-floor windows gain visible cross glazing bars and the ground-floor storefront glass picks up fine mullion lines, giving the openings the paned look of the concept, and the silhouette, colours and the rest of the facade are unchanged.

job: JOB 5: Hanging lanterns inside windows, porch glazing and shaft landings
why: Small hanging lanterns now sit inside the upper windows, porch glazing and shaft landings, echoing the warm interior glow of the concept without cluttering the facade or altering the silhouette, though they are tiny and sparse compared to the concept's lighting.

job: JOB 6: Wall lanterns on brackets, piers and the dark shaft pier
why: The small lanterns on brackets and piers match the concept's lantern detail, but at this scale they read as tiny sparse specks that barely change the silhouette or finish, and the added shaft-pier lanterns add little crafted depth.

job: JOB 7: Teal hanging banners either side of the doors, lanterns below
why: The banners now read as a messy teal-and-tan striped patch with a stray lantern hanging off the column edge and slight cut-away artifacts, instead of the clean teal banners with lanterns beneath that the concept shows.

job: JOB 8: Pier capitals and base blocks (Greek-key relief)
why: The before and after crops look essentially identical, so the Greek-key pier capitals and base blocks are not visible at this scale and the change adds neither crafted detail nor clutter.

job: JOB 9: Eave cornice and string-course bands
why: The porch gains a toothed, dentil-style cornice with a clear shadow line that echoes the concept's crowning detail, and the rest of the facade stays clean with no stray blocks or silhouette damage.

job: JOB 10: Pediment raking trim, stepped diagonal timber band
why: The 'after' raking band is thinner, broken into ragged half-height steps and partly buried or lost in dark shading, so the pediment's diagonal timber reads less crisp and less like the concept's bold stepped trim.

job: JOB 11: Spire finial on the pediment apex
why: A slim gold finial now rises from the pediment apex in both views, which echoes the spire in the concept and adds a crafted top note without disturbing the silhouette or colours.

job: JOB 12: Finial on the side gable
why: The finial is a bright orange-red ball on a thin stalk that clashes with the dark slate and gold palette, whereas the concept's finials are slender gold spires, and it sits as a floating-looking speck on the roof edge.

job: JOB 13: Pediment louvre slot
why: The thin wood louvre slats sit inside the pediment's dark recess, adding a bit of crafted depth and echoing the concept's slatted vent without breaking the silhouette, though the effect is subtle and a little sparse.

job: JOB 14: Tower-head louvred vent
why: The change adds only a faint lighter-plank streak variation to the existing wooden vent slot with no new profile, depth, or silhouette change, so it is barely visible and doesn't noticeably bring the tower head closer to the concept.

job: JOB 15: Tower-top railing
why: The added fences and posts around the tower top form a cluttered, spiky tangle (stray pickets poking above the merlons, uneven cross-bars in the elevation) rather than a clean railing, and the concept shows a simple tidy rail, so the silhouette and finish get messier.

job: JOB 16: Flagpole rod on the tower corner
why: the job changed no visible pixels in any view

job: JOB 17: Chimney stack with cap
why: The chimney stack is a flat-topped column of bright light-grey blocks that clashes with the dark deepslate, and its pale cap is stuck onto a stray single-block fragment in the roof silhouette rather than reading as a believable chimney.

job: JOB 18: Entrance steps with timber handrails
why: The thin timber handrails beside the entrance steps are a faithful nod to the concept but are barely visible at this scale. They sit as two small sticks that cast slightly odd shadows and add little depth or crafted finish, and they don't break the silhouette.

job: JOB 19: Lamp posts at the foot of the steps and by the plinth
why: The lamp posts add tiny, thin posts with lanterns at the plinth ends and foot of the steps, matching the concept's lanterns in spirit, but they are barely visible at this scale and sit awkwardly on the plinth edge rather than flanking the steps, so the change is minor and doesn't clearly improve or hurt the build.

job: JOB 20: Porch columns, capitals and transom
why: The change adds a darker transom band and a two-pane lintel above the doors, plus slightly more defined column and capital shading, which give the entrance more depth and finish and bring it closer to the concept's framed glazed doorway. The silhouette is intact and the colours match the existing palette.

job: JOB 21: Arched ground-floor windows with stone hood
why: The ground-floor windows get only a faint darker lintel strip above them in the close-ups, with no visible arched profile or stone hood depth, so the build reads essentially unchanged and nowhere near the concept's arched openings.

job: JOB 22: Flower planters and shrubs along the plinth and porch
why: The planters are only a few tiny dark-green and purple specks along the plinth edge and porch base, too small to read as the lush shrubs and flower beds in the concept, but they cause no damage to the silhouette or colours.

job: JOB 23: Mossy plinth and garden wall
why: The plinth gains a stone-brick base course with subtle mossy streaks and a continuous low wall that grounds the building and ties in with the concept's mossy foundation, with no damage to the silhouette or the facade.

job: JOB 24: Timber gate posts at the garden wall ends
why: The change adds two small tan timber posts at the garden wall ends, and they read as slightly thin stubs. They add a little finish, but they sit low and don't change the silhouette or the concept match.

job: JOB 25: Interior planters and shelving behind the glass
why: Bookshelves and small potted plants now sit behind the glass on the sill, adding interior depth and life to the windows as the concept shows, though the effect is tiny, limited to one window, and barely legible at distance.

job: JOB 26: Glass shaft mullion grid
why: The mullion grid in the glass shaft is only faintly different between before and after, with slightly darker, flatter glass and no real gain in crafted depth or in matching the concept's crisp mullioned shaft, but no clutter or silhouette damage either.

job: JOB 27: White quartz cap and bands on the shaft
why: The only visible change is a thin pale-grey band and a cap block inside the glass stair shaft, which reads as a small, slightly mismatched grey strip rather than the white quartz detailing in the concept, so it adds neither real crafted depth nor damage.

job: JOB 28: Corbelled balconies down the shaft side
why: The balconies gain corbelled undersides and a darker support course, giving the shaft-side platforms visible depth and weight that echo the concept's bracketed balconies, and the silhouette stays clean.

job: JOB 29: Fence-post colonnettes under the balconies
why: The thin fence-post colonnettes hanging under each balcony add supporting structure and depth that echo the concept's bracketed balconies, without cluttering the silhouette or clashing in colour.

job: JOB 30: External timber stair posts and rail
why: A thin dark timber post-and-rail strip appears in the recess beside the stair shaft; it adds a faint vertical line but is barely visible, low-contrast against the deepslate, and doesn't visibly add depth or move the build closer to the concept's stair detailing.

job: JOB 31: Dark downpipe beside the shaft
why: The black downpipe beside the shaft was replaced by a dull pair of thin tan posts that don't read as a dark downpipe, so the change adds clutter and the wrong colour without any gain in crafted detail or closeness to the concept.

job: JOB 32: Side service door with stone arch
why: The change swaps a few dark wall blocks beside the dark-wood door for lighter stone brick, which is a faint jamb-like accent, but no arch profile or depth is visible in this crop and the door reads almost the same as before.

job: JOB 33: Stair-stepped roof edge
why: The change adds a dark stepped cap and a ridge-top rail strip, plus slightly darker crenellations on the tower, but it's barely visible at this scale and doesn't add the concept's gable stair-stepping or clear depth, while also not breaking the silhouette.

job: JOB 34: Wall texture, weathering and variation
why: Subtle stone variation (mossy/cracked mottling) breaks up the flat deepslate on walls, piers and the shaft without touching the silhouette, trim or colours, which moves it toward the concept's weathered masonry, though the effect is sparse and slightly speckled.

job: JOB 35: Sides and back, window lintels and frames
why: The before/after crops look nearly identical, with only faint lintel and frame darkening on the side windows and no visible new depth, profile, or colour; the change is harmless but doesn't read as more crafted or closer to the concept.
